issues.text: The counterfactual assumes that, absent the AMC, PCV adoption would have followed the same path as Rotavirus vaccine adoption in the same countries. The evaluator argues this is not necessarily valid because the vaccines have different manufacturers with different willingness to supply low-income countries, and they impact different diseases with different relative treatment priorities.
issues.quote: the authors assume that, absent the AMC, PCV adoption would have followed the same path as Rotavirus vaccine adoption in the same countries. While this is a reasonable baseline, there are many reasons why that may not be the case.

issues.text: The evaluator suggests an alternative counterfactual construction, using each country's coverage of other GAVI-supported vaccines and PCV coverage in non-eligible countries, which the paper does not explore and which would be a useful direction for future research.
issues.quote: Perhaps constructing a counterfactual using each country\'s coverage of additional GAVI supported vaccines and using data on PCV coverage in countries that are not eligible for the AMC could be useful.

issues.text: The paper does not address whether the AMC is a permanent mechanism or a temporary one to promote adoption. Because vaccines require indefinite annual spending, the evaluator notes it is unclear how to fund an AMC in perpetuity or how to transition off it.
issues.quote: it would be valuable to consider if the AMC is a permanent mechanism or one used to promote the adoption of a vaccine. Since adoption of a vaccine usually necessitates large annual expenditures indefinitely

issues.text: Country co-financing requirements are intended to become self-financed over time, so removing them may be more costly than the model assumes; the model may understate these costs.
issues.quote: Therefore, the cost of removing county co-financing requirements may be larger than the model assumes.

issues.text: The theoretical model is one-shot, whereas in reality there are multiple bargaining periods in which manufacturers may reject early offers and accept higher ones later. The evaluator argues this makes the risk of setting the price too low initially less important than the model implies.
issues.quote: the model is a one-shot model, but, in reality, there can be multiple bargaining periods and manufacturers may initially reject offers but then accept higher offers in later periods.

issues.text: The model assumes manufacturers are strictly profit maximizing, whereas manufacturers are often constrained by social pressures to offer affordable prices. The evaluator notes the paper does not explore how these pressures affect bargaining over price.
issues.quote: manufactures are not strictly profit maximizing but are constrained by social pressures to provide vaccines at an affordable price. It would be useful to understand how these pressures impact the ability of the manufacturer to bargain over the vaccine price.
